 Flash-flood threat continues in the Southwest, but outlook is improving 
 New Mexico's San Juan River reached its highest crest since 1935. 
 1:49 Flooding occurred in Shiprock, New Mexico, when the San Juan River crested, October 24, 2026, to its highest level since 1935, overflowing its banks, officials said. Navajo Police Department By Kyle Reiman and Bill Hutchinson October 25, 2026, 3:24 PM Share Parts of the Southwest could see more flash flooding Sunday after heavy rains caused flooding on Saturday in New Mexico and Colorado.
 While the severe storm threat is less today, some storms Sunday afternoon and evening could be strong enough to produce gusty winds, isolated large hail and possible tornadoes.
 The flash flood threat continues, October 25, 2026, with a level 2 of 4 flood threat from western Texas up to southwest Kansas. ABC News A large area stretching from western Texas up into southwest Kansas is under a level 2 out of 4 threat Sunday for flooding.
 Possible rainfall rates in parts of the Southwest could reach 2 inches per hour later Sunday.
 Related October nor'easter pummeling Mid-Atlantic coast with high winds and large waves Due to the ground being saturated from consecutive days of heavy rain across the region, the threshold for flash flooding is low for these areas, meaning it wouldn't take much rain to cause rapid flash flooding.
 The flood threat from Western Texas to southwest Kansas is expected to start winding down Monday, but some spotty flooding is still possible.
 Flooding occurred in Shiprock, New Mexico, when the San Juan River crested, October 24, 2026, to its highest level since 1935, overflowing its banks, officials said. Navajo Police Department On Saturday, the San Juan River in New Mexico crested at 21 feet, the highest recorded crest since 1935, causing the river to overflow its banks and flood neighborhoods in Shiprock.
 Onshore flow brings high-tide flooding to Southeast coast
 In the Southeast, persistent onshore winds are expected to produce gusty winds and coastal flooding on Sunday.

 An area of high pressure over the Northeast, combined with a non-tropical low-pressure system in the Atlantic, are creating a corridor of persistent winds blowing onshore over the Southeast coast.
 Gusts of 20 to 35 mph are possible along the coast from Sunday to Tuesday.
 Flood alerts remain in place, October 25, 2026, for the Southeast coastline from Miami to Hatteras, North Carolina. ABC News The blustery conditions, combined with king tides in the area -- the highest high tides of the year -- have prompted coastal flood alerts through Tuesday from Miami to North Carolina's Outer Banks.
 Southeast Florida, from Port St. Lucie to Miami, is under a level 2 out of 4 flash-flood threat on Sunday.
 Flash flooding threat along Florida's east coastline, October 25, 2026. ABC News Minor to moderate flooding is expected to occur during high tide, with major high-tide flooding possible for parts of the Florida and Georgia coasts.
 Rough surf, rip currents and waves up to 12 feet are also possible in coastal waters from Florida to the Carolinas through Tuesday.
